title: More German than many Germans
excerpt: I just wanted to do an internship in Europe so it would be easier to find a job after graduation. That internship completely changed my life.
content_html:
In 2017, after I finished the third year of my Computer Science studies, I decided to do an internship in Europe. So while I was applying for the Erasmus Scholarship, I also started looking for internships. In the end I got the scholarship, which helped a lot with the visa process, and I also found an internship at a company in Hamburg.

I had never been outside of Turkey before. So I had also never really talked to people from other countries. What I knew about Germans came mostly from the Turkish people who moved to Germany in the 60s for work. Those people came back to Turkey almost every summer and told us about their life there. Most of what they said was the same as what you can read on the internet, the stereotypical German.

People who don't laugh, who are cold and unfriendly, who always follow the rules, who speak a language that sounds too harsh, and so on. And of course, someone always brings up the Nazis.

Apart from the people I talked to in the interviews, my first real contact was my German flatmate. Before I arrived he showed me the room on Skype and we agreed on it. When I landed in Hamburg, he picked me up from the airport. That was a great start, and during my three months there we chatted in the kitchen almost every evening for half an hour.

I had a lot of questions for him and he always answered them properly. On the weekends he picked up his girlfriend and they either stayed home or went rowing. Their relationship looked very healthy to me. She was studying medicine, so sometimes she was working at her desk on a Saturday while my flatmate played Witcher 3 right next to her. I never heard them argue about anything.

Near the end of my internship he told me that he and his girlfriend were going to Africa, so I would be alone in the flat for a week. When I asked him what I should do with the keys, he just said to drop them in the mailbox. That much trust after such a short time really surprised me.

We had a last dinner together and I told him things were going well at the company and there was a chance I could come back to Hamburg.

I was lucky with my flatmate and I was also lucky at work. I had a great team. They taught me new things, gave me responsibilities the other summer interns didn't get, and included me in all the team events. The offsite we had outside the city is something I still remember today. And I was getting all of this while earning minimum wage.

I was really surprised by how friendly everyone was. We weren't just working, we were having fun. Everything I had heard about Germans until that point was gone. It was the best summer of my life.

My lead was happy with my work and offered me a job right away. I could work as a freelancer from Turkey while finishing my studies, and if they were happy with my performance I would get a full-time contract. That is what happened.

Coming back

In April 2018 I got my contract, even before I finished my studies. The next month something nice happened. My German flatmate emailed me and asked when I was coming back, because he already had a room for me for the summer. The company was going to give me a place to stay, but I couldn't say no to him. Right after my last exam, before I even had my diploma, I moved to Hamburg at the end of June and started working full time with the same team, living with the same flatmate.

On my first day there were candies and balloons on my desk. Everybody was happy to see me again. One colleague who knew my interest in Apple gave me a German flag pin he got at WWDC18. He said he tried to swap it for a Turkish flag but couldn't manage it. I was already happy with the gift, because it meant he was thinking about me while he was in California.

When you start living in Germany you have to register your address. When I went to the public office, the clerk told me I had already lived in Hamburg before. I said I had done a summer internship a year earlier. He just said: Welcome back!

That was the moment I felt like I was coming home, not moving to a new country.

The first years

My first months were mostly about finding a flat and figuring out how things work here. Since my German wasn't good enough, my colleagues came with me to flat viewings after work. When I had a problem with my electricity provider, a colleague came along and did all the talking. When I moved to a different place a year later, a German colleague rented a van and helped me carry everything.

At the time, the company was one of the biggest internet companies here, with around 2.000 people. Sometimes I saw the C-level in the kitchen getting their own coffee or even washing their own glasses. They had assistants, but the assistants helped with work instead of acting like servants. We also had a CFO who rode a very old bike to the office.

Whenever we had a team event or an offsite, the organisers made sure they knew everyone's dietary needs. Vegan, vegetarian, halal, no alcohol, allergies. So everyone would have something to eat and drink.

When I was doing a good job, my lead kept telling me to take vacation instead of working more. When I was sick, he told me to stay home until I felt better. I didn't even need a doctor's note. It took me a while to notice this was not only a work thing. You get on a bus or a train here and nobody checks your ticket. I wasn't used to this level of trust.

Across from our office there was an Italian restaurant where we went for pizza sometimes. The pizzas were very tasty and huge, and it was the only place that sold half a pizza. At lunch I saw people in suits eating there, and right at the next table people from the construction site nearby in their work clothes eating the same pizza. Nobody looked at the other table and nobody thought it was worth noticing except me. That is the part that stayed with me. It was completely normal, and it was normal because a man who spent his morning on a building site can afford an Italian lunch and eat it like everyone else.

I noticed the same thing in the rich districts of Hamburg. You can walk into one and not feel like you don't belong, and the prices in the shops are not that different from anywhere else in the city. Sometimes they are exactly the same. The more I saw of that, the more I wanted to stay. I believe in social democracy, and this is a country that calls itself one and mostly behaves like it.

It didn't take long for me to move up at work. I didn't feel any discrimination, even though people say Germans prefer Germans when it comes to promotions. There were already a lot of people with a migration background at the top. When I ran as a candidate in the works council election, I got the most votes of anyone, even though there were many Germans running and only around 25% of the company were immigrants like me.

You see the same thing outside of companies. Cem Özdemir, whose parents came from Turkey, has been the prime minister of Baden-Württemberg since May. Sinan Selen, who was born in Istanbul, runs the office for the protection of the constitution.

Being in the works council gave me more contact with the C-level. Sometimes I found myself arguing with the CTO or the CEO, and later at a company party we would have a beer together and talk about something else. That is when I understood how flat the management is here. I saw the difference later when I worked for an American company, where they made sure you knew you were lower on the ladder.

I met hundreds of Germans at that company and they were always super friendly. I say this because years later I still see many of my old colleagues at different events, and most of my friends today are people I used to work with. A lot of immigrants complain that it is hard to become friends with Germans, but that wasn't my experience.

My landing was soft

I should be honest about one thing here. I landed softly. I came into a big international company where everyone spoke English, in a city like Hamburg, with a salary that let me pick where I live. I have worked with other German companies since then, mostly smaller ones, so what I write here is not only about that one place. But the start was much easier for me than it is for most people. A lot of them arrive with none of that, and the country they meet is not the same one I met. Everything I write here is my experience, not a report on how it works for everyone.

The language is part of that. Every story I told above happened in English. The team, the flatmate, the works council, the arguments with the CEO, all of it. Once I decided I was going to stay here for a long time, I started taking German classes, and after the citizenship law changed I put much more effort into it. So the German came from the decision to stay. It was not the thing that made me stay.

I never really tried to integrate. It just happened that the way I think about life turned out to be similar to how people here think.

Why I like the rules

Most people complain about the rules in Germany, but I like them. It means someone, or a group of people, sat down and thought about that specific thing and decided on a standard for everyone. When you have to do something, you don't feel lost, because you can just look it up. You don't have to find someone who knows.

Rules also make normal days easier. Something simple like waiting at a red light even when there are no cars takes away the work of deciding whether to cross. And if everyone does it, you don't have to worry about someone suddenly stepping into the street. Or the fire safety rule that makes exit doors in public buildings open outwards. You never have to think about pull or push.

There are also unwritten rules, like being on time. For me the logical thing has always been to aim for 15 minutes before the agreed time, so if something happens on the way I'm still fine. After going on dates with a lot of Germans, I realised they do the same thing. So instead of me arriving early and waiting 15 minutes, we just meet 15 minutes earlier.

My favourite one is Ruhezeit, the quiet time between 10PM and 6AM, plus Sundays and public holidays. My sleep is very important to me and I'm a light sleeper, so this rule really helps me. Sometimes I had neighbours who had parties during those hours, and I didn't hesitate to complain (with Lärmprotokoll) to my landlord. Many Germans have told me I'm more German than many Germans. It is probably because of examples like this one.

The one time a rule was pointed at me instead of working for me was my first application for permanent residence. I had just left my first company and I was between jobs, and that was enough to get it rejected. That was when I learned what a sustainable livelihood means to the German authorities. It doesn't mean the money you have in your account. It means a permanent contract with the probation time already behind you. I had savings and it didn't count for anything.

It was an emotional day. But after I calmed down I could see their logic. A bank balance can be gone in a year and a signed contract that already survived six months says something a number can't. It was the same system I like for every other reason, just this time I was on the wrong side of it.

Understanding the country

The longer I lived here, the more I saw myself spending the rest of my life here. That made me want to read about the country. I'm a heavy reader and I track every book, so here are the ones I read about Germany:

  • German Men Sit Down To Pee & Other Insights Into German Culture
  • Germany: Memories of a Nation
  • The German Genius
  • Kaput: The End of the German Miracle
  • Man's Search for Meaning
  • Blood and Iron: The Rise and Fall of the German Empire 1871 to 1918
  • Why the Germans Do it Better: Notes from a Grown-Up Country

Apart from the books, I also watched a lot of documentaries, especially about the Nazi era.

Like most people, I didn't know that Germany wasn't one country until the 19th century. It was made of small kingdoms, city states and so on. That is why there are so many kinds of bread, beer and sausage, why some parts have different public holidays, different accents and even a different way of living.

The German Genius surprised me the most. It is about 1.000 pages about Germans who contributed to humanity in different fields, and I didn't know how many things in our daily life exist thanks to them. Some of them had to escape the country because of the Nazis and reached their full potential somewhere else, in countries like the US and the UK. The books also helped me understand how Germany built an educated middle class, how workers' rights and social reforms happened, and where the rule about no shopping on Sundays comes from.

What stayed with me is that this is probably the only country in the western world that faced its own history properly, admitted the worst things it did, and built a lot of its identity around not repeating them. You feel that here in small ways, not only in museums. In January 2024, after it came out that far right politicians had talked about deporting people who already hold a German passport, 50.000 to 80.000 people filled the streets of my city in one afternoon.

In eight years I have not had a single case of racism. I know that isn't true for everyone, and I know the far right keeps growing.

I don't think most of those votes are about hating foreigners. Some people believe the story they get every day, that the country is broken and that immigrants are the problem. You find that story almost everywhere. The rest are angry that certain problems here have not been solved for years by the existing parties, so they look for an alternative.

For me, Germans are people who give trust before it is earned. People who are friendly without being fake about it. People who make sure everyone is included, down to what is on the table. People who care about someone they will never meet. People who know exactly what happened here and don't look away from it.

Making it official

That is why I decided to become one of them.

The chance came when the traffic light coalition, which I think was the most progressive government this country has had in decades, changed the citizenship rules and brought the waiting time down to five years. I was eligible, so I applied.

People seem to think a German passport is handed out easily now. It isn't. You have to prove you paid into the social system for at least five years. You have to pass the citizenship test. You need German at B1 level. You need a sustainable livelihood while your application is running. And most importantly, you have to accept the democratic values of this country.

For me the process itself was smooth. I applied online by uploading a pile of PDFs. A week later I got a letter saying my application had arrived, with a few papers to sign, scan and upload back. Then the waiting started. In total it took around 14 months to get the email saying my application was successful and that I could come and collect my Einbürgerungsurkunde.

I picked it up this week, at an appointment that only took 15 minutes. I am German now.

I believe I have contributed something to this society in these eight years and I will keep doing it. And I will keep complaining about everything that needs to be better. Because that is what real Germans do.

sentences.zh: 除了采访中交谈过的人之外，我第一个真正接触到的是我的德国室友。

sentences.en: Before I arrived he showed me the room on Skype and we agreed on it.
sentences.zh: 在我到达之前，他在 Skype 上向我展示了房间，我们同意了。

sentences.en: When I landed in Hamburg, he picked me up from the airport.
sentences.zh: 当我抵达汉堡时，他到机场接我。

sentences.en: That was a great start, and during my three months there we chatted in the kitchen almost every evening for half an hour.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的开始，在那里的三个月里，我们几乎每天晚上都在厨房里聊天半个小时。

blocks.html_en: I had a lot of questions for him and he always answered them properly. On the weekends he picked up his girlfriend and they either stayed home or went rowing. Their relationship looked very healthy to me. She was studying medicine, so sometimes she was working at her desk on a Saturday while my flatmate played Witcher 3 right next to her. I never heard them argue about anything.

sentences.en: I had a lot of questions for him and he always answered them properly.
sentences.zh: 我有很多问题想问他，他总是给出正确的答案。

sentences.en: On the weekends he picked up his girlfriend and they either stayed home or went rowing.
sentences.zh: 周末他会去接女朋友，他们要么呆在家里，要么去划船。

sentences.en: Their relationship looked very healthy to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他们的关系非常健康。

sentences.en: She was studying medicine, so sometimes she was working at her desk on a Saturday while my flatmate played Witcher 3 right next to her.
sentences.zh: 她正在学习医学，所以有时周六她会在办公桌前工作，而我的室友就在她旁边玩《巫师 3》。

sentences.en: I never heard them argue about anything.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有听到他们争论任何事。

blocks.html_en: Near the end of my internship he told me that he and his girlfriend were going to Africa, so I would be alone in the flat for a week. When I asked him what I should do with the keys, he just said to drop them in the mailbox. That much trust after such a short time really surprised me.

sentences.en: Near the end of my internship he told me that he and his girlfriend were going to Africa, so I would be alone in the flat for a week.
sentences.zh: 实习快结束时，他告诉我他和他的女朋友要去非洲，所以我会独自在公寓里呆一个星期。

sentences.en: When I asked him what I should do with the keys, he just said to drop them in the mailbox.
sentences.zh: 当我问他应该如何处理钥匙时，他只是说把它们放在邮箱里。

sentences.en: That much trust after such a short time really surprised me.
sentences.zh: 这么短的时间后得到的如此多的信任确实让我感到惊讶。

blocks.html_en: We had a last dinner together and I told him things were going well at the company and there was a chance I could come back to Hamburg.

sentences.en: We had a last dinner together and I told him things were going well at the company and there was a chance I could come back to Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 我们一起吃了最后一顿晚餐，我告诉他公司一切进展顺利，我有机会回到汉堡。

blocks.html_en: I was lucky with my flatmate and I was also lucky at work. I had a great team. They taught me new things, gave me responsibilities the other summer interns didn't get, and included me in all the team events. The offsite we had outside the city is something I still remember today. And I was getting all of this while earning minimum wage.

sentences.en: I was lucky with my flatmate and I was also lucky at work.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运有我的室友，我的工作也很幸运。

sentences.en: I had a great team.
sentences.zh: 我有一支很棒的团队。

sentences.en: They taught me new things, gave me responsibilities the other summer interns didn't get, and included me in all the team events.
sentences.zh: 他们教了我新东西，给了我其他暑期实习生没有得到的责任，并让我参加了所有的团队活动。

sentences.en: The offsite we had outside the city is something I still remember today.
sentences.zh: 我至今仍记得我们在城外的异地。

sentences.en: And I was getting all of this while earning minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 我在赚取最低工资的同时得到了这一切。

sentences.en: My first offsite event
sentences.zh: 我的第一次场外活动

blocks.html_en: I was really surprised by how friendly everyone was. We weren't just working, we were having fun. Everything I had heard about Germans until that point was gone. It was the best summer of my life.

sentences.en: I was really surprised by how friendly everyone was.
sentences.zh: 我真的很惊讶每个人都如此友好。

sentences.en: We weren't just working, we were having fun.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅在工作，而且在享受乐趣。

sentences.en: Everything I had heard about Germans until that point was gone.
sentences.zh: 在那之前我所听到的关于德国人的一切都消失了。

sentences.en: It was the best summer of my life.
sentences.zh: 那是我一生中最美好的夏天。

blocks.html_en: My lead was happy with my work and offered me a job right away. I could work as a freelancer from Turkey while finishing my studies, and if they were happy with my performance I would get a full-time contract. That is what happened.

sentences.en: My lead was happy with my work and offered me a job right away.
sentences.zh: 我的领导对我的工作很满意，并立即给了我一份工作。

sentences.en: I could work as a freelancer from Turkey while finishing my studies, and if they were happy with my performance I would get a full-time contract.
sentences.zh: 我可以在完成学业的同时作为来自土耳其的自由职业者工作，如果他们对我的表现感到满意，我将获得一份全职合同。

sentences.en: That is what happened.
sentences.zh: 这就是发生的事情。

blocks.html_en: Coming back

sentences.en: Coming back
sentences.zh: 回来了

blocks.html_en: In April 2018 I got my contract, even before I finished my studies. The next month something nice happened. My German flatmate emailed me and asked when I was coming back, because he already had a room for me for the summer. The company was going to give me a place to stay, but I couldn't say no to him. Right after my last exam, before I even had my diploma, I moved to Hamburg at the end of June and started working full time with the same team, living with the same flatmate.

sentences.en: In April 2018 I got my contract, even before I finished my studies.
sentences.zh: 2018 年 4 月，我在完成学业之前就拿到了合同。

sentences.en: The next month something nice happened.
sentences.zh: 接下来的一个月发生了一些好事。

sentences.en: My German flatmate emailed me and asked when I was coming back, because he already had a room for me for the summer.
sentences.zh: 我的德国室友给我发了电子邮件，问我什么时候回来，因为他已经为我准备了一个夏天的房间。

sentences.en: The company was going to give me a place to stay, but I couldn't say no to him.
sentences.zh: 公司要给我一个住处，但我不能拒绝他。

sentences.en: Right after my last exam, before I even had my diploma, I moved to Hamburg at the end of June and started working full time with the same team, living with the same flatmate.
sentences.zh: 就在我最后一次考试之后，在我拿到文凭之前，我于六月底搬到了汉堡，开始在同一个团队全职工作，和同一个室友住在一起。

blocks.html_en: On my first day there were candies and balloons on my desk. Everybody was happy to see me again. One colleague who knew my interest in Apple gave me a German flag pin he got at WWDC18. He said he tried to swap it for a Turkish flag but couldn't manage it. I was already happy with the gift, because it meant he was thinking about me while he was in California.

sentences.en: On my first day there were candies and balloons on my desk.
sentences.zh: 第一天，我的桌子上有糖果和气球。

sentences.en: Everybody was happy to see me again.
sentences.zh: 大家都很高兴再次见到我。

sentences.en: One colleague who knew my interest in Apple gave me a German flag pin he got at WWDC18.
sentences.zh: 一位知道我对 Apple 感兴趣的同事给了我一枚他在 WWDC18 上获得的德国国旗徽章。

sentences.en: He said he tried to swap it for a Turkish flag but couldn't manage it.
sentences.zh: 他说他试图把它换成土耳其国旗，但没成功。

sentences.en: I was already happy with the gift, because it meant he was thinking about me while he was in California.
sentences.zh: 我对这份礼物已经很满意了，因为这意味着他在加利福尼亚的时候一直在想着我。

sentences.en: My desk
sentences.zh: 我的办公桌

blocks.html_en: When you start living in Germany you have to register your address. When I went to the public office, the clerk told me I had already lived in Hamburg before. I said I had done a summer internship a year earlier. He just said: Welcome back!

sentences.en: When you start living in Germany you have to register your address.
sentences.zh: 当您开始在德国居住时，您必须注册您的地址。

sentences.en: When I went to the public office, the clerk told me I had already lived in Hamburg before.
sentences.zh: 当我去公共办公室时，工作人员告诉我，我以前已经住在汉堡了。

sentences.en: I said I had done a summer internship a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 我说我一年前做过暑期实习。

sentences.en: He just said: Welcome back!
sentences.zh: 他只是说：欢迎回来！

blocks.html_en: That was the moment I felt like I was coming home, not moving to a new country.

sentences.en: That was the moment I felt like I was coming home, not moving to a new country.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我感觉自己就像回到了家，而不是搬到了一个新的国家。

blocks.html_en: The first years

sentences.en: The first years
sentences.zh: 最初的几年

blocks.html_en: My first months were mostly about finding a flat and figuring out how things work here. Since my German wasn't good enough, my colleagues came with me to flat viewings after work. When I had a problem with my electricity provider, a colleague came along and did all the talking. When I moved to a different place a year later, a German colleague rented a van and helped me carry everything.

sentences.en: My first months were mostly about finding a flat and figuring out how things work here.
sentences.zh: 我的头几个月主要是寻找公寓并了解这里的运作方式。

sentences.en: Since my German wasn't good enough, my colleagues came with me to flat viewings after work.
sentences.zh: 由于我的德语不够好，我的同事下班后就陪我去看房。

sentences.en: When I had a problem with my electricity provider, a colleague came along and did all the talking.
sentences.zh: 当我与电力供应商发生问题时，一位同事过来并负责解决所有问题。

sentences.en: When I moved to a different place a year later, a German colleague rented a van and helped me carry everything.
sentences.zh: 一年后，当我搬到另一个地方时，一位德国同事租了一辆面包车并帮我搬运所有东西。

blocks.html_en: At the time, the company was one of the biggest internet companies here, with around 2.000 people. Sometimes I saw the C-level in the kitchen getting their own coffee or even washing their own glasses. They had assistants, but the assistants helped with work instead of acting like servants. We also had a CFO who rode a very old bike to the office.

sentences.en: At the time, the company was one of the biggest internet companies here, with around 2.000 people.
sentences.zh: 当时，该公司是这里最大的互联网公司之一，拥有约 2000 名员工。

sentences.en: Sometimes I saw the C-level in the kitchen getting their own coffee or even washing their own glasses.
sentences.zh: 有时我看到 C 级人员在厨房里自己煮咖啡，甚至自己洗杯子。

sentences.en: They had assistants, but the assistants helped with work instead of acting like servants.
sentences.zh: 他们有助理，但助理只是帮忙干活，而不是像仆人一样。

sentences.en: We also had a CFO who rode a very old bike to the office.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一位首席财务官，他骑着一辆非常旧的自行车去办公室。

blocks.html_en: Whenever we had a team event or an offsite, the organisers made sure they knew everyone's dietary needs. Vegan, vegetarian, halal, no alcohol, allergies. So everyone would have something to eat and drink.

sentences.en: Whenever we had a team event or an offsite, the organisers made sure they knew everyone's dietary needs.
sentences.zh: 每当我们举办团队活动或场外活动时，组织者都会确保他们了解每个人的饮食需求。

sentences.en: Vegan, vegetarian, halal, no alcohol, allergies.
sentences.zh: 素食、素食、清真、不含酒精、过敏。

sentences.en: So everyone would have something to eat and drink.
sentences.zh: 这样每个人都会有吃的、喝的。

blocks.html_en: When I was doing a good job, my lead kept telling me to take vacation instead of working more. When I was sick, he told me to stay home until I felt better. I didn't even need a doctor's note. It took me a while to notice this was not only a work thing. You get on a bus or a train here and nobody checks your ticket. I wasn't used to this level of trust.

sentences.en: When I was doing a good job, my lead kept telling me to take vacation instead of working more.
sentences.zh: 当我做得很好时，我的领导一直告诉我去休假而不是加班。

sentences.en: When I was sick, he told me to stay home until I felt better.
sentences.zh: 当我生病时，他告诉我待在家里直到我感觉好一些。

sentences.en: I didn't even need a doctor's note.
sentences.zh: 我什至不需要医生证明。

sentences.en: It took me a while to notice this was not only a work thing.
sentences.zh: 我花了一段时间才注意到这不仅仅是工作的事情。

sentences.en: You get on a bus or a train here and nobody checks your ticket.
sentences.zh: 你在这里乘坐公共汽车或火车，没有人检查你的车票。

sentences.en: I wasn't used to this level of trust.
sentences.zh: 我不习惯这种程度的信任。

sentences.en: My second offsite
sentences.zh: 我的第二次异地

blocks.html_en: Across from our office there was an Italian restaurant where we went for pizza sometimes. The pizzas were very tasty and huge, and it was the only place that sold half a pizza. At lunch I saw people in suits eating there, and right at the next table people from the construction site nearby in their work clothes eating the same pizza. Nobody looked at the other table and nobody thought it was worth noticing except me. That is the part that stayed with me. It was completely normal, and it was normal because a man who spent his morning on a building site can afford an Italian lunch and eat it like everyone else.

sentences.en: Across from our office there was an Italian restaurant where we went for pizza sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我们办公室对面有一家意大利餐厅，我们有时去那里吃披萨。

sentences.en: The pizzas were very tasty and huge, and it was the only place that sold half a pizza.
sentences.zh: 披萨非常好吃而且很大，而且这是唯一卖半个披萨的地方。

sentences.en: At lunch I saw people in suits eating there, and right at the next table people from the construction site nearby in their work clothes eating the same pizza.
sentences.zh: 午餐时，我看到穿着西装的人在那里吃饭，隔壁桌的人穿着工作服，从附近的建筑工地吃着同样的披萨。

sentences.en: Nobody looked at the other table and nobody thought it was worth noticing except me.
sentences.zh: 除了我之外，没有人看另一张桌子，也没有人认为它值得注意。

sentences.en: That is the part that stayed with me.
sentences.zh: 那是我一直铭记的部分。

sentences.en: It was completely normal, and it was normal because a man who spent his morning on a building site can afford an Italian lunch and eat it like everyone else.
sentences.zh: 这是完全正常的，这很正常，因为一个在建筑工地上度过一上午的人可以买得起意大利午餐，并且可以像其他人一样吃。

blocks.html_en: I noticed the same thing in the rich districts of Hamburg. You can walk into one and not feel like you don't belong, and the prices in the shops are not that different from anywhere else in the city. Sometimes they are exactly the same. The more I saw of that, the more I wanted to stay. I believe in social democracy, and this is a country that calls itself one and mostly behaves like it.

sentences.en: I noticed the same thing in the rich districts of Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 我在汉堡的富人区也注意到了同样的事情。

sentences.en: You can walk into one and not feel like you don't belong, and the prices in the shops are not that different from anywhere else in the city.
sentences.zh: 走进一家商店，你不会觉得自己不属于这里，而且商店里的价格与城里其他地方的价格并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Sometimes they are exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 有时它们是完全相同的。

sentences.en: The more I saw of that, the more I wanted to stay.
sentences.zh: 我看到的越多，我就越想留下来。

sentences.en: I believe in social democracy, and this is a country that calls itself one and mostly behaves like it.
sentences.zh: 我相信社会民主主义，这是一个自称为社会民主主义的国家，而且大多数人的行为也与它相似。

blocks.html_en: It didn't take long for me to move up at work. I didn't feel any discrimination, even though people say Germans prefer Germans when it comes to promotions. There were already a lot of people with a migration background at the top. When I ran as a candidate in the works council election, I got the most votes of anyone, even though there were many Germans running and only around 25% of the company were immigrants like me.

sentences.en: It didn't take long for me to move up at work.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，我的工作就得到了晋升。

sentences.en: I didn't feel any discrimination, even though people say Germans prefer Germans when it comes to promotions.
sentences.zh: 我没有感受到任何歧视，尽管人们说德国人在升职方面更喜欢德国人。

sentences.en: There were already a lot of people with a migration background at the top.
sentences.zh: 高层已经有很多有移民背景的人了。

sentences.en: When I ran as a candidate in the works council election, I got the most votes of anyone, even though there were many Germans running and only around 25% of the company were immigrants like me.
sentences.zh: 当我作为候选人参加劳资委员会选举时，我获得了最多的选票，尽管有很多德国人参加竞选，而且公司中只有大约 25% 的员工是像我这样的移民。

blocks.html_en: You see the same thing outside of companies. Cem Özdemir, whose parents came from Turkey, has been the prime minister of Baden-Württemberg since May. Sinan Selen, who was born in Istanbul, runs the office for the protection of the constitution.

sentences.en: You see the same thing outside of companies.
sentences.zh: 在公司之外你也会看到同样的事情。

sentences.en: Cem Özdemir, whose parents came from Turkey, has been the prime minister of Baden-Württemberg since May.
sentences.zh: 杰姆·厄兹德米尔（Cem Özdemir）的父母来自土耳其，自五月以来一直担任巴登-符腾堡州总理。

sentences.en: Sinan Selen, who was born in Istanbul, runs the office for the protection of the constitution.
sentences.zh: 出生于伊斯坦布尔的锡南·塞伦（Sinan Selen）负责宪法保护办公室。

blocks.html_en: Being in the works council gave me more contact with the C-level. Sometimes I found myself arguing with the CTO or the CEO, and later at a company party we would have a beer together and talk about something else. That is when I understood how flat the management is here. I saw the difference later when I worked for an American company, where they made sure you knew you were lower on the ladder.

sentences.en: Being in the works council gave me more contact with the C-level.
sentences.zh: 加入劳资委员会让我与高管层有了更多的接触。

sentences.en: Sometimes I found myself arguing with the CTO or the CEO, and later at a company party we would have a beer together and talk about something else.
sentences.zh: 有时我发现自己在与首席技术官或首席执行官争论，后来在公司聚会上我们会一起喝啤酒并谈论其他事情。

sentences.en: That is when I understood how flat the management is here.
sentences.zh: 那时我才明白这里的管理是多么扁平化。

sentences.en: I saw the difference later when I worked for an American company, where they made sure you knew you were lower on the ladder.
sentences.zh: 后来当我在一家美国公司工作时，我看到了其中的差异，他们确保你知道自己的职位较低。

blocks.html_en: I met hundreds of Germans at that company and they were always super friendly. I say this because years later I still see many of my old colleagues at different events, and most of my friends today are people I used to work with. A lot of immigrants complain that it is hard to become friends with Germans, but that wasn't my experience.

sentences.en: I met hundreds of Germans at that company and they were always super friendly.
sentences.zh: 我在那家公司遇到了数百名德国人，他们总是非常友好。

sentences.en: I say this because years later I still see many of my old colleagues at different events, and most of my friends today are people I used to work with.
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为多年后我仍然在不同的活动中见到许多老同事，而今天我的大多数朋友都是我曾经共事过的人。

sentences.en: A lot of immigrants complain that it is hard to become friends with Germans, but that wasn't my experience.
sentences.zh: 很多移民抱怨很难与德国人成为朋友，但这不是我的经历。

blocks.html_en: My landing was soft

sentences.en: My landing was soft
sentences.zh: 我的着陆很软

blocks.html_en: I should be honest about one thing here. I landed softly. I came into a big international company where everyone spoke English, in a city like Hamburg, with a salary that let me pick where I live. I have worked with other German companies since then, mostly smaller ones, so what I write here is not only about that one place. But the start was much easier for me than it is for most people. A lot of them arrive with none of that, and the country they meet is not the same one I met. Everything I write here is my experience, not a report on how it works for everyone.

sentences.en: I should be honest about one thing here.
sentences.zh: 我应该诚实地讲一件事。

sentences.en: I landed softly.
sentences.zh: 我轻轻落地。

sentences.en: I came into a big international company where everyone spoke English, in a city like Hamburg, with a salary that let me pick where I live.
sentences.zh: 我进入了一家大型国际公司，在汉堡这样的城市，每个人都说英语，我的薪水让我可以选择居住的地方。

sentences.en: I have worked with other German companies since then, mostly smaller ones, so what I write here is not only about that one place.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我曾与其他德国公司合作过，大多是规模较小的公司，所以我在这里写的不仅仅是那个地方。

sentences.en: But the start was much easier for me than it is for most people.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，开始比对大多数人来说要容易得多。

sentences.en: A lot of them arrive with none of that, and the country they meet is not the same one I met.
sentences.zh: 他们中的很多人抵达时都没有这些，而且他们遇到的国家与我遇到的国家不一样。

sentences.en: Everything I write here is my experience, not a report on how it works for everyone.
sentences.zh: 我在这里写的所有内容都是我的经验，而不是关于它如何适用于每个人的报告。

blocks.html_en: The language is part of that. Every story I told above happened in English. The team, the flatmate, the works council, the arguments with the CEO, all of it. Once I decided I was going to stay here for a long time, I started taking German classes, and after the citizenship law changed I put much more effort into it. So the German came from the decision to stay. It was not the thing that made me stay.

sentences.en: The language is part of that.
sentences.zh: 语言是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Every story I told above happened in English.
sentences.zh: 我上面讲的每个故事都是用英语发生的。

sentences.en: The team, the flatmate, the works council, the arguments with the CEO, all of it.
sentences.zh: 团队、室友、工作委员会、与首席执行官的争论，所有这些。

sentences.en: Once I decided I was going to stay here for a long time, I started taking German classes, and after the citizenship law changed I put much more effort into it.
sentences.zh: 当我决定要在这里长期居住时，我开始上德语课，公民法改变后我投入了更多的努力。

sentences.en: So the German came from the decision to stay.
sentences.zh: 于是德国人就做出了留下来的决定。

sentences.en: It was not the thing that made me stay.
sentences.zh: 这并不是让我留下来的原因。

blocks.html_en: I never really tried to integrate. It just happened that the way I think about life turned out to be similar to how people here think.

sentences.en: I never really tried to integrate.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有真正尝试过融入。

sentences.en: It just happened that the way I think about life turned out to be similar to how people here think.
sentences.zh: 碰巧我对生活的看法和这里的人的想法很相似。

blocks.html_en: Why I like the rules

sentences.en: Why I like the rules
sentences.zh: 为什么我喜欢规则

blocks.html_en: Most people complain about the rules in Germany, but I like them. It means someone, or a group of people, sat down and thought about that specific thing and decided on a standard for everyone. When you have to do something, you don't feel lost, because you can just look it up. You don't have to find someone who knows.

sentences.en: Most people complain about the rules in Germany, but I like them.
sentences.zh: 大多数人抱怨德国的规则，但我喜欢它们。

sentences.en: It means someone, or a group of people, sat down and thought about that specific thing and decided on a standard for everyone.
sentences.zh: 这意味着某人或一群人坐下来思考特定的事情并为每个人确定一个标准。

sentences.en: When you have to do something, you don't feel lost, because you can just look it up.
sentences.zh: 当你必须做某事时，你不会感到迷失，因为你可以查找它。

sentences.en: You don't have to find someone who knows.
sentences.zh: 你不必找认识的人。

blocks.html_en: Rules also make normal days easier. Something simple like waiting at a red light even when there are no cars takes away the work of deciding whether to cross. And if everyone does it, you don't have to worry about someone suddenly stepping into the street. Or the fire safety rule that makes exit doors in public buildings open outwards. You never have to think about pull or push.

sentences.en: Rules also make normal days easier.
sentences.zh: 规则也让日常生活变得更加轻松。

sentences.en: Something simple like waiting at a red light even when there are no cars takes away the work of deciding whether to cross.
sentences.zh: 一些简单的事情，比如在没有车辆的情况下等红灯，就可以省去决定是否过马路的麻烦。

sentences.en: And if everyone does it, you don't have to worry about someone suddenly stepping into the street.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都这样做，你就不必担心有人突然走进街上。

sentences.en: Or the fire safety rule that makes exit doors in public buildings open outwards.
sentences.zh: 或者公共建筑的出口门向外打开的消防安全规则。

sentences.en: You never have to think about pull or push.
sentences.zh: 你永远不必考虑拉或推。

blocks.html_en: There are also unwritten rules, like being on time. For me the logical thing has always been to aim for 15 minutes before the agreed time, so if something happens on the way I'm still fine. After going on dates with a lot of Germans, I realised they do the same thing. So instead of me arriving early and waiting 15 minutes, we just meet 15 minutes earlier.

sentences.en: There are also unwritten rules, like being on time.
sentences.zh: 还有一些不成文的规则，比如准时。

sentences.en: For me the logical thing has always been to aim for 15 minutes before the agreed time, so if something happens on the way I'm still fine.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，合乎逻辑的事情一直是在约定时间之前 15 分钟到达，所以如果途中发生什么事情我也没关系。

sentences.en: After going on dates with a lot of Germans, I realised they do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 在与很多德国人约会后，我意识到他们也做同样的事情。

sentences.en: So instead of me arriving early and waiting 15 minutes, we just meet 15 minutes earlier.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不用提前到达并等待 15 分钟，而是提前 15 分钟见面。

blocks.html_en: My favourite one is Ruhezeit, the quiet time between 10PM and 6AM, plus Sundays and public holidays. My sleep is very important to me and I'm a light sleeper, so this rule really helps me. Sometimes I had neighbours who had parties during those hours, and I didn't hesitate to complain (with Lärmprotokoll) to my landlord. Many Germans have told me I'm more German than many Germans. It is probably because of examples like this one.

sentences.en: My favourite one is Ruhezeit, the quiet time between 10PM and 6AM, plus Sundays and public holidays.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是 Ruhezeit，晚上 10 点到早上 6 点之间的安静时间，以及周日和公众假期。

sentences.en: My sleep is very important to me and I'm a light sleeper, so this rule really helps me.
sentences.zh: 我的睡眠对我来说非常重要，而且我睡眠很浅，所以这条规则对我很有帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes I had neighbours who had parties during those hours, and I didn't hesitate to complain (with Lärmprotokoll) to my landlord.
sentences.zh: 有时我的邻居在这些时间里举办聚会，我会毫不犹豫地向房东投诉（与 Lärmprotokoll）。

sentences.en: Many Germans have told me I'm more German than many Germans.
sentences.zh: 许多德国人告诉我，我比许多德国人更像德国人。

sentences.en: It is probably because of examples like this one.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为像这样的例子。

blocks.html_en: The one time a rule was pointed at me instead of working for me was my first application for permanent residence. I had just left my first company and I was between jobs, and that was enough to get it rejected. That was when I learned what a sustainable livelihood means to the German authorities. It doesn't mean the money you have in your account. It means a permanent contract with the probation time already behind you. I had savings and it didn't count for anything.

sentences.en: The one time a rule was pointed at me instead of working for me was my first application for permanent residence.
sentences.zh: 一次规则针对我而不是为我工作是我第一次申请永久居留。

sentences.en: I had just left my first company and I was between jobs, and that was enough to get it rejected.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚离开我的第一家公司，而且我正在换工作，这足以让我被拒绝。

sentences.en: That was when I learned what a sustainable livelihood means to the German authorities.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我了解到可持续生计对德国当局意味着什么。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean the money you have in your account.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着您帐户中的资金。

sentences.en: It means a permanent contract with the probation time already behind you.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一份永久合同，试用期已经过去。

sentences.en: I had savings and it didn't count for anything.
sentences.zh: 我有积蓄，但它没有任何意义。

blocks.html_en: It was an emotional day. But after I calmed down I could see their logic. A bank balance can be gone in a year and a signed contract that already survived six months says something a number can't. It was the same system I like for every other reason, just this time I was on the wrong side of it.

sentences.en: It was an emotional day.
sentences.zh: 这是激动人心的一天。

sentences.en: But after I calmed down I could see their logic.
sentences.zh: 但当我冷静下来之后，我就明白了他们的逻辑。

sentences.en: A bank balance can be gone in a year and a signed contract that already survived six months says something a number can't.
sentences.zh: 银行存款可能会在一年内耗尽，而一份已经签署了六个月的合同却说明了​​一些数字所无法做到的事情。

sentences.en: It was the same system I like for every other reason, just this time I was on the wrong side of it.
sentences.zh: 这与我出于其他原因喜欢的系统是一样的，只是这一次我站在了错误的一边。

sentences.zh: 了解国家

blocks.html_en: The longer I lived here, the more I saw myself spending the rest of my life here. That made me want to read about the country. I'm a heavy reader and I track every book, so here are the ones I read about Germany:

sentences.en: The longer I lived here, the more I saw myself spending the rest of my life here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里住的时间越长，我就越能看到自己在这里度过余生。

sentences.en: That made me want to read about the country.
sentences.zh: 这让我想了解这个国家。

sentences.en: I'm a heavy reader and I track every book, so here are the ones I read about Germany:
sentences.zh: 我是一个重度读者，我会跟踪每一本书，所以以下是我读过的关于德国的书：

sentences.en: The German Genius
sentences.zh: 德国天才

sentences.zh: 卡普特：德国奇迹的终结

sentences.zh: 人类寻找意义

sentences.zh: 为什么德国人做得更好：来自一个发达国家的笔记

blocks.html_en: Apart from the books, I also watched a lot of documentaries, especially about the Nazi era.

sentences.en: Apart from the books, I also watched a lot of documentaries, especially about the Nazi era.
sentences.zh: 除了书之外，我还看了很多纪录片，尤其是关于纳粹时代的纪录片。

blocks.html_en: Like most people, I didn't know that Germany wasn't one country until the 19th century. It was made of small kingdoms, city states and so on. That is why there are so many kinds of bread, beer and sausage, why some parts have different public holidays, different accents and even a different way of living.

sentences.en: Like most people, I didn't know that Germany wasn't one country until the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 和大多数人一样，直到 19 世纪我才知道德国不是一个国家。

sentences.en: It was made of small kingdoms, city states and so on.
sentences.zh: 它是由小王国、城邦等组成的。

sentences.en: That is why there are so many kinds of bread, beer and sausage, why some parts have different public holidays, different accents and even a different way of living.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有这么多种类的面包、啤酒和香肠，为什么有些地方有不同的公共假期，不同的口音，甚至不同的生活方式。

blocks.html_en: The German Genius surprised me the most. It is about 1.000 pages about Germans who contributed to humanity in different fields, and I didn't know how many things in our daily life exist thanks to them. Some of them had to escape the country because of the Nazis and reached their full potential somewhere else, in countries like the US and the UK. The books also helped me understand how Germany built an educated middle class, how workers' rights and social reforms happened, and where the rule about no shopping on Sundays comes from.

sentences.en: The German Genius surprised me the most.
sentences.zh: 德国天才最令我惊讶。

sentences.en: It is about 1.000 pages about Germans who contributed to humanity in different fields, and I didn't know how many things in our daily life exist thanks to them.
sentences.zh: 这本书大约有1000页，讲述了德国人在不同领域为人类做出的贡献，我不知道我们的日常生活中有多少事情是由于他们而存在的。

sentences.en: Some of them had to escape the country because of the Nazis and reached their full potential somewhere else, in countries like the US and the UK.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人因为纳粹而不得不逃离这个国家，并在其他国家（例如美国和英国）充分发挥自己的潜力。

sentences.en: The books also helped me understand how Germany built an educated middle class, how workers' rights and social reforms happened, and where the rule about no shopping on Sundays comes from.
sentences.zh: 这些书还帮助我了解德国如何建立受过教育的中产阶级，工人权利和社会改革如何发生，以及周日禁止购物的规定从何而来。

blocks.html_en: What stayed with me is that this is probably the only country in the western world that faced its own history properly, admitted the worst things it did, and built a lot of its identity around not repeating them. You feel that here in small ways, not only in museums. In January 2024, after it came out that far right politicians had talked about deporting people who already hold a German passport, 50.000 to 80.000 people filled the streets of my city in one afternoon.

sentences.en: What stayed with me is that this is probably the only country in the western world that faced its own history properly, admitted the worst things it did, and built a lot of its identity around not repeating them.
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的是，这可能是西方世界中唯一一个正确面对自己的历史、承认自己做过的最糟糕的事情、并围绕不重蹈覆辙建立自己的身份的国家。

sentences.en: You feel that here in small ways, not only in museums.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以通过一些小方式感受到这一点，而不仅仅是在博物馆里。

sentences.en: In January 2024, after it came out that far right politicians had talked about deporting people who already hold a German passport, 50.000 to 80.000 people filled the streets of my city in one afternoon.
sentences.zh: 2024 年 1 月，当极右政客谈论驱逐已经持有德国护照的人的消息传出后，一个下午就有 5 万到 8 万人挤满了我所在城市的街道。

sentences.en: In eight years I have not had a single case of racism.
sentences.zh: 八年来我没有遇到过一例种族主义事件。

sentences.en: I know that isn't true for everyone, and I know the far right keeps growing.

sentences.en: People who are friendly without being fake about it.

sentences.en: People who make sure everyone is included, down to what is on the table.

content_html_zh:
2017年，当我完成计算机科学第三年的学习后，我决定去欧洲实习。 所以在我申请伊拉斯谟奖学金的同时，我也开始寻找实习机会。 最终我获得了奖学金，这对签证过程有很大帮​​助，而且我还找到了汉堡一家公司的实习机会。

我以前从未出过土耳其。 所以我也从未真正与其他国家的人交谈过。 我对德国人的了解主要来自于 60 年代移居德国工作的土耳其人。 这些人几乎每年夏天都会回到土耳其，向我们讲述他们在那里的生活。 他们所说的大部分内容与您在互联网上读到的内容相同，是典型的德国人。

不笑的人、冷漠、不友好的人、总是遵守规则的人、说着听起来太刺耳的语言的人，等等。 当然，总会有人提起纳粹。

除了采访中交谈过的人之外，我第一个真正接触到的是我的德国室友。 在我到达之前，他在 Skype 上向我展示了房间，我们同意了。 当我抵达汉堡时，他到机场接我。 这是一个很好的开始，在那里的三个月里，我们几乎每天晚上都在厨房里聊天半个小时。

我有很多问题想问他，他总是给出正确的答案。 周末他会去接女朋友，他们要么呆在家里，要么去划船。 在我看来，他们的关系非常健康。 她正在学习医学，所以有时周六她会在办公桌前工作，而我的室友就在她旁边玩《巫师 3》。 我从来没有听到他们争论任何事。

实习快结束时，他告诉我他和他的女朋友要去非洲，所以我会独自在公寓里呆一个星期。 当我问他应该如何处理钥匙时，他只是说把它们放在邮箱里。 这么短的时间后得到的如此多的信任确实让我感到惊讶。

我们一起吃了最后一顿晚餐，我告诉他公司一切进展顺利，我有机会回到汉堡。

我很幸运有我的室友，我的工作也很幸运。 我有一支很棒的团队。 他们教了我新东西，给了我其他暑期实习生没有得到的责任，并让我参加了所有的团队活动。 我至今仍记得我们在城外的异地。 我在赚取最低工资的同时得到了这一切。

我真的很惊讶每个人都如此友好。 我们不仅在工作，而且在享受乐趣。 在那之前我所听到的关于德国人的一切都消失了。 那是我一生中最美好的夏天。

我的领导对我的工作很满意，并立即给了我一份工作。 我可以在完成学业的同时作为来自土耳其的自由职业者工作，如果他们对我的表现感到满意，我将获得一份全职合同。 这就是发生的事情。

回来了

2018 年 4 月，我在完成学业之前就拿到了合同。 接下来的一个月发生了一些好事。 我的德国室友给我发了电子邮件，问我什么时候回来，因为他已经为我准备了一个夏天的房间。 公司要给我一个住处，但我不能拒绝他。 就在我最后一次考试之后，在我拿到文凭之前，我于六月底搬到了汉堡，开始在同一个团队全职工作，和同一个室友住在一起。

第一天，我的桌子上有糖果和气球。 大家都很高兴再次见到我。 一位知道我对 Apple 感兴趣的同事给了我一枚他在 WWDC18 上获得的德国国旗徽章。 他说他试图把它换成土耳其国旗，但没成功。 我对这份礼物已经很满意了，因为这意味着他在加利福尼亚的时候一直在想着我。

当您开始在德国居住时，您必须注册您的地址。 当我去公共办公室时，工作人员告诉我，我以前已经住在汉堡了。 我说我一年前做过暑期实习。 他只是说：欢迎回来！

那一刻我感觉自己就像回到了家，而不是搬到了一个新的国家。

最初的几年

我的头几个月主要是寻找公寓并了解这里的运作方式。 由于我的德语不够好，我的同事下班后就陪我去看房。 当我与电力供应商发生问题时，一位同事过来并负责解决所有问题。 一年后，当我搬到另一个地方时，一位德国同事租了一辆面包车并帮我搬运所有东西。

当时，该公司是这里最大的互联网公司之一，拥有约 2000 名员工。 有时我看到 C 级人员在厨房里自己煮咖啡，甚至自己洗杯子。 他们有助理，但助理只是帮忙干活，而不是像仆人一样。 我们还有一位首席财务官，他骑着一辆非常旧的自行车去办公室。

每当我们举办团队活动或场外活动时，组织者都会确保他们了解每个人的饮食需求。 素食、素食、清真、不含酒精、过敏。 这样每个人都会有吃的、喝的。

当我做得很好时，我的领导一直告诉我去休假而不是加班。 当我生病时，他告诉我待在家里直到我感觉好一些。 我什至不需要医生证明。 我花了一段时间才注意到这不仅仅是工作的事情。 你在这里乘坐公共汽车或火车，没有人检查你的车票。 我不习惯这种程度的信任。

我们办公室对面有一家意大利餐厅，我们有时去那里吃披萨。 披萨非常好吃而且很大，而且这是唯一卖半个披萨的地方。 午餐时，我看到穿着西装的人在那里吃饭，隔壁桌的人穿着工作服，从附近的建筑工地吃着同样的披萨。 除了我之外，没有人看另一张桌子，也没有人认为它值得注意。 那是我一直铭记的部分。 这是完全正常的，这很正常，因为一个在建筑工地上度过一上午的人可以买得起意大利午餐，并且可以像其他人一样吃。

我在汉堡的富人区也注意到了同样的事情。 走进一家商店，你不会觉得自己不属于这里，而且商店里的价格与城里其他地方的价格并没有什么不同。 有时它们是完全相同的。 我看到的越多，我就越想留下来。 我相信社会民主主义，这是一个自称为社会民主主义的国家，而且大多数人的行为也与它相似。

没过多久，我的工作就得到了晋升。 我没有感受到任何歧视，尽管人们说德国人在升职方面更喜欢德国人。 高层已经有很多有移民背景的人了。 当我作为候选人参加劳资委员会选举时，我获得了最多的选票，尽管有很多德国人参加竞选，而且公司中只有大约 25% 的员工是像我这样的移民。

在公司之外你也会看到同样的事情。 杰姆·厄兹德米尔（Cem Özdemir）的父母来自土耳其，自五月以来一直担任巴登-符腾堡州总理。 出生于伊斯坦布尔的锡南·塞伦（Sinan Selen）负责宪法保护办公室。

加入劳资委员会让我与高管层有了更多的接触。 有时我发现自己在与首席技术官或首席执行官争论，后来在公司聚会上我们会一起喝啤酒并谈论其他事情。 那时我才明白这里的管理是多么扁平化。 后来当我在一家美国公司工作时，我看到了其中的差异，他们确保你知道自己的职位较低。

我在那家公司遇到了数百名德国人，他们总是非常友好。 我这么说是因为多年后我仍然在不同的活动中见到许多老同事，而今天我的大多数朋友都是我曾经共事过的人。 很多移民抱怨很难与德国人成为朋友，但这不是我的经历。

我的着陆很软

我应该诚实地讲一件事。 我轻轻落地。 我进入了一家大型国际公司，在汉堡这样的城市，每个人都说英语，我的薪水让我可以选择居住的地方。 从那时起，我曾与其他德国公司合作过，大多是规模较小的公司，所以我在这里写的不仅仅是那个地方。 但对我来说，开始比对大多数人来说要容易得多。 他们中的很多人抵达时都没有这些，而且他们遇到的国家与我遇到的国家不一样。 我在这里写的所有内容都是我的经验，而不是关于它如何适用于每个人的报告。

语言是其中的一部分。 我上面讲的每个故事都是用英语发生的。 团队、室友、工作委员会、与首席执行官的争论，所有这些。 当我决定要在这里长期居住时，我开始上德语课，公民法改变后我投入了更多的努力。 于是德国人就做出了留下来的决定。 这并不是让我留下来的原因。

我从来没有真正尝试过融入。 碰巧我对生活的看法和这里的人的想法很相似。

为什么我喜欢规则

大多数人抱怨德国的规则，但我喜欢它们。 这意味着某人或一群人坐下来思考特定的事情并为每个人确定一个标准。 当你必须做某事时，你不会感到迷失，因为你可以查找它。 你不必找认识的人。

规则也让日常生活变得更加轻松。 一些简单的事情，比如在没有车辆的情况下等红灯，就可以省去决定是否过马路的麻烦。 如果每个人都这样做，你就不必担心有人突然走进街上。 或者公共建筑的出口门向外打开的消防安全规则。 你永远不必考虑拉或推。

还有一些不成文的规则，比如准时。 对我来说，合乎逻辑的事情一直是在约定时间之前 15 分钟到达，所以如果途中发生什么事情我也没关系。 在与很多德国人约会后，我意识到他们也做同样的事情。 因此，我们不用提前到达并等待 15 分钟，而是提前 15 分钟见面。

我最喜欢的是 Ruhezeit，晚上 10 点到早上 6 点之间的安静时间，以及周日和公众假期。 我的睡眠对我来说非常重要，而且我睡眠很浅，所以这条规则对我很有帮助。 有时我的邻居在这些时间里举办聚会，我会毫不犹豫地向房东投诉（与 Lärmprotokoll）。 许多德国人告诉我，我比许多德国人更像德国人。 可能是因为像这样的例子。

一次规则针对我而不是为我工作是我第一次申请永久居留。 我刚刚离开我的第一家公司，而且我正在换工作，这足以让我被拒绝。 就在那时，我了解到可持续生计对德国当局意味着什么。 这并不意味着您帐户中的资金。 这意味着一份永久合同，试用期已经过去。 我有积蓄，但它没有任何意义。

这是激动人心的一天。 但当我冷静下来之后，我就明白了他们的逻辑。 银行存款可能会在一年内耗尽，而一份已经签署了六个月的合同却说明了​​一些数字所无法做到的事情。 这与我出于其他原因喜欢的系统是一样的，只是这一次我站在了错误的一边。

了解国家

我在这里住的时间越长，我就越能看到自己在这里度过余生。 这让我想了解这个国家。 我是一个重度读者，我会跟踪每一本书，所以以下是我读过的关于德国的书：

  • 德国男人坐下来小便以及对德国文化的其他见解
  • 德国：一个民族的记忆
  • 德国天才
  • 卡普特：德国奇迹的终结
  • 人类寻找意义
  • 血与铁：1871年至1918年德意志帝国的兴衰
  • 为什么德国人做得更好：来自一个发达国家的笔记

除了书之外，我还看了很多纪录片，尤其是关于纳粹时代的纪录片。

和大多数人一样，直到 19 世纪我才知道德国不是一个国家。 它是由小王国、城邦等组成的。 这就是为什么有这么多种类的面包、啤酒和香肠，为什么有些地方有不同的公共假期，不同的口音，甚至不同的生活方式。

德国天才最令我惊讶。 这本书大约有1000页，讲述了德国人在不同领域为人类做出的贡献，我不知道我们的日常生活中有多少事情是由于他们而存在的。 他们中的一些人因为纳粹而不得不逃离这个国家，并在其他国家（例如美国和英国）充分发挥自己的潜力。 这些书还帮助我了解德国如何建立受过教育的中产阶级，工人权利和社会改革如何发生，以及周日禁止购物的规定从何而来。

让我印象深刻的是，这可能是西方世界中唯一一个正确面对自己的历史、承认自己做过的最糟糕的事情、并围绕不重蹈覆辙建立自己的身份的国家。 在这里，你可以通过一些小方式感受到这一点，而不仅仅是在博物馆里。 2024 年 1 月，当极右政客谈论驱逐已经持有德国护照的人的消息传出后，一个下午就有 5 万到 8 万人挤满了我所在城市的街道。

八年来我没有遇到过一例种族主义事件。 我知道并非所有人都这样，而且我知道极右翼势力在不断壮大。

我不认为这些选票大部分是关于仇恨外国人的。 有些人相信他们每天听到的故事，即国家已经崩溃，移民是问题所在。 你几乎到处都能找到这个故事。 其他人对现有政党多年来未能解决某些问题感到愤怒，因此他们寻找替代方案。

对我来说，德国人是先给予信任再赢得信任的人。 人们友善而不虚伪。 他们确保每个人都参与其中，具体到桌面上的内容。 那些在乎一个他们永远不会见面的人。 人们清楚地知道这里发生了什么，并且不会将目光移开。

使其正式化

这就是为什么我决定成为他们中的一员。

当红绿灯联盟——我认为是这个国家几十年来最进步的政府——改变了公民身份规则并将等待时间缩短到五年时，机会来了。 我符合资格，所以我申请了。

人们似乎认为现在发放德国护照很容易。 事实并非如此。 您必须证明您已向社会系统缴纳了至少五年的费用。 您必须通过公民考试。 您需要 B1 水平的德语。 当您的应用程序运行时，您需要可持续的生计。 最重要的是，你必须接受这个国家的民主价值观。

对我来说，这个过程本身很顺利。 我是通过上传一堆PDF文件在线申请的。 一周后，我收到一封信，说我的申请已经到达，还有一些文件需要签名、扫描并上传回来。 然后等待就开始了。 总共花了大约 14 个月的时间才收到一封电子邮件，告知我的申请已成功，我可以来领取我的 Einbürgerungsurkunde。

我这周就收到了它，预约只用了 15 分钟。 我现在是德国人了。

我相信这八年来我为这个社会做出了一些贡献，我会继续这样做。 我会继续抱怨一切需要改进的地方。 因为这就是真正的德国人所做的。
